title: Finite closed-intersection primitives and normalized inverse-image compositors
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $A$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], actual inverse/direct images [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] and their unit-normalized adjunctions [def-sfb-proetale-unit-normalized-adjunction]. For a finite ordered family $W_a\to X$ and a finite subset $s$, define $Z_s$ as the finite product in $\operatorname{Sch}/X$, using chosen fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]; the empty product is $X$. For a scheme map $f$ define $E_f=f_*f^*$ and its actual unit. Pullback of an ordered family is the family of fibre products. Pullback of a complex applies module inverse image degreewise. For successive maps $T\xrightarrow{g}Y\xrightarrow{h}X$, define the ring compositor $(hg)^{-1}A\cong g^{-1}h^{-1}A$ as the adjunction conjugate of sectionwise fibre-product pasting. Define the module compositor $(hg)^*M\cong g^*h^*M$, with scalars restricted along that ring compositor, by its unique characterization carrying original unit sections to successive unit sections. No existence of a resolution or exactness is part of these definitions.
